六级大纲词汇 · 13英文原文

The Call Before the Hurdle

过栏前的那声提醒 · 590 词 · 7 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1A polytechnic held a tournament with a relay across low hurdles. Ben had entered as an alternate. He became a starter after the captain hurt his leg in a wrestling bout. The last leg was a formidable assignment for a timid runner. A teammate called their adversary ruthless. Ben needed that mindset, he said. Ben's aspiration was simpler. In a team beset by antagonism, he wanted one clean handover. He asked which call to wait for.

2At first he tried to cram a fortnight of practice into two evenings. He clenched his jaw and ran until his legs quivered. His coach made him alternate a slow lap with a fast one. The alternation let him feel where his foot should land. He learned to crouch at a mark and let a call propel him forward. Then he turned too early, hit a hurdle, and limped away panting. The humiliation hurt more than the bruise. He expected a blunt reproach. A teammate offered flattery instead.

3The coach would not flatter him. She wanted him to wrestle with the timing. Conceit would be as useless as panic. She asked what he had heard just before the fall. It was his teammate's long shout, which had started before the runner was close. They tried a short call in consecutive sessions. The tactic restored morale. A conceited teammate still teased Ben about looking too feminine for the arena. His idea of a masculine temperament left no room for fear. To him, masculinity meant hiding it. Ben watched an ardent supporter help a rival lace a shoe. The courtesy seemed more confident than the stereotype.

4On race day restless spectators crowded the barrier. Noise from the cricket field began to agitate younger runners. The rival began to dart forward before his partner reached the exchange zone. Ben kept his poise and waited for the agreed call. The rival tried to dodge someone behind him and slammed a hand into the ground. Ben avoided a shove but lost momentum. His teammate had started to stumble. Ben held his arm still rather than jerk it away. The other boy caught up and drove the baton into his palm.

5They finished second. The referee asked whether Ben had seen a lane violation. Ben felt a brief thrill at being able to change the result. The sensation passed. He had no wish to humiliate a rival he respected. He said the contact had been trivial. The team conceded the result, and the referee commended him for speaking precisely. The injured captain offered a compliment for waiting. It would once have sounded like consolation. Now he knew how waiting had kept them in the race.

6At the next session a young lad arrived with more zeal than patience. Ben tucked the baton under his arm and put one hurdle at its lowest setting. He showed him the mark where he had fallen. No one needed to aspire to a trophy before trying the movement. The only prerequisite was listening for the call. When the boy managed it, Ben felt his weariness lift. He had equated dedication with relentless practice alone. It could also mean staying long enough for a teammate to learn one thing well.

7It was the culmination of their work in adversity. Winning would have felt good, but complacency could undo it all. Ben still wanted a trophy. For now he asked the boy to call once more. He had the boy stand behind him. Ben waited until it was close. He hoped neither would forget that pause.

过栏前的那声提醒

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1一所理工学院举办运动会，其中一项是低栏接力。本原本报的是替补，队长在摔跤比赛里伤了腿，他才成了正式队员。对一个胆小的跑手来说，跑最后一棒是个难题。队友说对手冷酷无情，本也得有这种心态。本想要的简单得多。队里已经有不少敌意，他只想完成一次利落的交棒，便问起跑前该听什么口令。

2起初，他想把两周的训练塞进两个晚上。他咬着牙跑，跑到两腿发抖。教练让他慢跑一圈，再快跑一圈，交替进行。这样他能感觉出脚该落在哪里。他学会在标记处蹲下，听见口令后往前冲。有一回他转身太早，撞到栏架，一瘸一拐地离开跑道，喘个不停。丢脸的感觉比瘀伤还疼。他以为会听见直截了当的责备，一位队友却奉承了他几句。

3教练不肯说好听话。她想让本弄清起跑的时机。自大和慌张一样，都帮不上忙。她问本摔倒前听到了什么。队友还离得远就拖长声音喊了他。接下来的几次训练，他们改用短口令，队伍的士气也回来了。一名自负的队友还嘲笑本，说他上场太像女孩子。在那名队友看来，男子汉不能显得害怕。本却看见一个热心的支持者帮对手系鞋带。这样的礼貌，比那种成见更显得从容。

4比赛当天，躁动的观众挤在护栏边。旁边板球场的喧闹，让几个年轻跑手有些慌。对方跑手的搭档还没到交接区，他就开始向前冲。本稳住了，等约定的口令。对手想躲开身后的人，一只手重重拍在地上。本避开了推挤，却丢了速度。他的队友也绊了一下。本伸出的手没有猛地缩回去。队友追上来，把接力棒送进他掌心。

5他们得了第二名。裁判问本有没有看到对方串道。想到自己的回答可能改变结果，本一时有些兴奋，随即平静下来。他敬重对方，不想让对手难堪，便如实说那只是轻微接触。全队接受了结果，裁判称赞他说得准确。受伤的队长也夸他肯等。过去，他可能只把这话当安慰。现在他知道，正是那一等让他们能把比赛跑完。

6下一次训练，一名年轻队员干劲十足，却没什么耐心。本把接力棒夹在胳膊下，把一个栏架降到最低，指给他看自己摔倒的位置。要练会这个动作，不必先想着拿奖杯。先学会听口令就行。男孩做成时，本觉得疲惫消散了。他曾以为投入就是独自拼命练习。如今他发现，留下来陪队友练好一件事，也是投入。

7这是他们在困难中坚持训练得到的结果。赢下来当然痛快，但一旦自满，练出来的东西也会丢掉。本还是想拿奖杯。眼下，他让男孩站在自己身后，再喊一遍口令。本等到声音接近了才动。他希望两个人都能记得那短短的一等。
